department: College of Agriculture and Environmental Sciences

deadline.value: General Fall priority admission and merit-based funding deadline is January 15 (applied automatically with the admission application); general international Fall deadline is May 15.
deadline.quote: Priority Admission Application Deadline / Priority Funding Deadline (applies only to Fall semester admissions): January 15 | International Student Admission Application Deadline: May 15

gre_general.value: A GRE Aptitude Exam score is required for admission to the Sustainable Agriculture and Environmental Sciences concentration of the Ph.D. program.
gre_general.quote: Additional Admission Requirements | A Graduate Record Exam (GRE) Aptitude Exam score

gre_subject.value: ETS does not offer a GRE Subject Test in Environmental Sciences.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Neither the CAES Ph.D. program page nor the Sustainable Agriculture & Environmental Sciences catalog entry states a pre-admission supervisor requirement.

funding.value: Applicants who apply by the priority deadline are automatically considered for Graduate College Doctoral GTAs ($20,000 minimum 9-month stipend, full tuition, and student health insurance for 1 year, renewable up to 2 years, followed by faculty grant GRAs), though currently only a portion of qualified students are funded.
funding.quote: Doctoral Graduate Teaching Assistants (GTAs): doctoral student support will be paid by The Graduate College, and include tuition in the amount for a full time student, health insurance, and a nine month stipend at a minimum of $20,000. This package is a one-year commitment that can be renewed for a maximum of two years. | However, currently only a portion of qualified students will be supported as GTAs.

also.quote: Students who apply late have significantly reduced chances of receiving funding as offers are made to eligible students on a first-come, first-serve basis.

entry_route.value: Applicants must hold an earned master's degree in a food, agricultural, biological science, environmental science, or closely related discipline with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.3.
entry_route.quote: To gain admission to this agricultural and environmental sciences Ph.D. program, students must have earned a master’s degree in a food, agricultural, biological science or environmental science discipline or in a closely related area of study with a cumulative GPA of 3.3.

notes: Includes five concentrations, notably Sustainable Agriculture and Environmental Sciences (plus Food Science, Agribusiness, Animal Health, and Agricultural & Extension Education).
